title: N44 in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The southern part of N44 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: Large Magellanic Cloud, LMC, N 44 · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This picture shows the southern part of N44, an H II region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a neighboring galaxy of the Milky Way.

An H II region is a cloud of hydrogen gas that has been ionized by the energetic light of hot, young stars. When the atoms in the gas recapture electrons, they give off light at particular wavelengths, which is why such clouds glow. Regions like this are signposts of recent star formation.

The colors carry a clue. According to the caption, the green areas are particularly hot. The camera, the Wide Field Imager on ESO's 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla, recorded the scene through narrow filters that isolate light from oxygen and from hydrogen, so different colors in the image trace different gases and conditions. The field measures 27.5 by 26.5 arcminutes, with north up and east to the left. The official caption offers few further details.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (32.28 x 32.38 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 1,600 × 1,600 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager uses narrow filters for two kinds of oxygen light and for hydrogen-alpha. The caption says green marks particularly hot areas, but the full filter-to-color mapping is not published.
understand.eye: The narrow filters isolate individual gases rather than showing the colors an eye would see, and long exposures reveal very faint gas.

alt: Glowing gas in the southern part of the N44 region, with green highlighting particularly hot areas.
